title: Rollout Timing Cheat Sheet and Hotfix Plan
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal reference for staged rollouts, when to pin, and the emergency hotfix path. Keep this short and actionable — copy into runbook when stable.

Context / intent:
- Target deliverable: bump serving-runtime to v6.2.0 with KV cache fix and kernel selection tweak (PR 1782).
- Primary risk: subtle latency regressions at p95 under mixed short/long sequences.
- Secondary risk: increased OOMs for 16GB VM pool on heavy batch windows.
- Goal: get 30% traffic on new binary within 2 hours if metrics look good, ramp to 100% by EOD.

Quick checklist (pre-roll):
- [ ] CI green + perf benchmark summary attached to PR (look for p50/p95/cost-per-token).
- [ ] Canary image pushed to staging registry tag: serving-runtime:v6.2.0-canary-20260312.
- [ ] Smoke test: run internal harness (scripts/smoke_canary.sh) against staging for 5m.
- [ ] Alert page updated: #incidents + oncall notified (pager: Ethan).
- [ ] Pin plan recorded in rollout ticket and pinned in Console (see commands below).

Canary schedule (default):
- minute 0: route 0.5% traffic to canary cohort across 3 regions (NA / EU / AP) evenly.
- minute 15: if no spikes, increase to 2%.
- minute 45: move to 8% and enable broader telemetry (extra traces, kv cache hit ratio).
- minute 90: if stable, 30% and monitor for 1h.
- hour 4 onward: progressive increments 30 -> 60 -> 100 over remaining business day if stable.

Hard thresholds (abort / rollback):
- latency: p95 increases by >30% vs baseline for 10m window -> immediate rollback.
- errors: 5xx rate >0.5% absolute increase for 5m -> rollback.
- OOMs: any OOM observed in dedicated pool for 3+ containers within 10m -> immediate rollback and notify infra.
- cost: token cost spike >20% (unlikely) -> pause and investigate.

Monitoring queries (copy to alerts):
- p95 latency (PromQL): 100 * (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)))
- 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
- kv cache hit ratio: sum(kv_cache_hits) / sum(kv_cache_requests)
- OOMs: increase in container_restart_count{reason="OOMKilled"} over 10m

Pinning / emergency pin commands (console & CLI examples):
- Console: Product -> Models -> serving-runtime -> Pin version v6.1.9 for customer cohorts A,B (use sticky routing).
- CLI (redwoodctl placeholder):
  redwoodctl rollout create --model serving-runtime --version v6.2.0 --cohort canary --traffic 0.5 --region global --note "canary initial"
  redwoodctl pin set --service serving-runtime --version v6.1.9 --cohorts A,B,C --reason "rollback after latency spike"
- NOTE: pin is sticky; communicate in #releases before applying.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Pause all automated ramps in Console.
2) Execute pin command to previous stable (v6.1.9).
3) Route 100% of canary cohort back to pinned version.
4) Open incident, attach logs, and collect flamegraphs (upload to S3 under incidents/ENG-5942/).
5) Run binary diff script locally (tools/binary-diff.sh) to confirm changed kernels.
6) If OOMs, temporarily increase worker memory or decrease batch_size on the pool; inform SRE.

Hotfix patch plan (if rollback shows config bug):
- If root cause is config (batching / autobalance), push config-only hotfix to canary: serving-runtime:v6.2.1-config.
- If root cause is code, triage with @Ethan and @Liang (APPLIED-ML) and open fast-track PR with test harness attached.
- Communication: post update in #releases, mention affected customers, and update status page if SLA impacted.

Observability notes (what to inspect first):
- Trace samples around requests that hit p95 to see KV cache behavior.
- Compare batch sizes distribution (shouldn’t shift drastically after kernel tweak).
- Check routing logs — ensure user cohorts got expected variants.
- Look for any host-level metrics (GPU memory, kernel time) that deviate from baseline.

Post-roll validation (after reaching 100%):
- Collect 24h perf summary and compare p50/p95/p99 to baseline. Save as artifacts to PR.
- Run regression test set (evals/regression_suite/2026-02) and confirm no >3% quality drop on checks.
- Annotate PR with final numbers and close rollout ticket.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want automated slow-roll for model-heavy customers? (ticket: ENG-5968)
- Add canary cohort that uses only long-sequence traffic? Useful to detect latency regressions earlier.
- Should Console allow auto-pin-on-failure? Pros/cons: safety vs. accidental pins.

Notes to self / shortcuts:
- If in a hurry: pin first, then run investigation (less customer impact).
- When paging SRE include: cluster, pool id, observed OOM counts, relevant commit SHA.
- Keep this doc short; if pattern repeats, move it into releases/runbook/pinning.md in shared_drives.

History:
- 2026-02-12: initial draft after staging perf run (Ava).
- 2026-03-13: updated thresholds after last month's canary (minor relax on p95 threshold).

---
Small personal reminder: breathe. During ramps, console looks boring for long stretches — set a 15m timer to re-check metrics.
